newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa edges up, March/March switch active.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa edges up, March/March switch active.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures edged up slightly in very routine, rangebound trade dominated by March/March switches, traders said.
"The market is just dead, trading in narrow ranges," said one. The only dominant feature was the March 1997/March 1998 switches which were traded at around 71 stg.
The deals were done this morning and a further volume was noted in the afternoon, traders said.
By the close, nearby March was two stg up at 932 a tonne after ranging within a narrow five stg band.
Overall volume was 2,428 lots, with the nearby March accounting for 1,193.
Without major market-moving news, traders said the market could see low volumes of industry or fund buying until the end of the year.
"We haven't seen good quality buying from the industry for some time now," one said. "Until we have good quality buying I think the market will hold on the level."
He saw funds holding on to current positions, but not building any new big positions until early 1997.

In fundamental news, the head of Ghana's Cocoa Board told reporters at International Cocoa Organisation meeting in London that the country's total crop would be between 320,000 and 340,000 tonnes in the current 1996/97 season, down from 400,000 last season.
Traders said the forecast was within trade expectation.

But Malaysian crop could be higher at 130,000 against 126,000 in the previous season, a Malaysian official told Reuters. Production is expected to steadily increase to 150,000 by 1998/99, this source said.
